html:
On the 1783 map, Lahore stands for the Punjab around the city of Lahore, then held by Sikh chiefs after the Mughals and Afghans lost their grip. The shape also reaches north into the hills toward Kashmir.

Lahore had been one of the great cities of the Mughal Empire, with a royal fort and the Badshahi Mosque. In the 1700s the Punjab became a battleground. Ahmad Shah Durrani invaded again and again from Afghanistan, while Sikh bands grew into a loose league of chiefdoms, the misls. In 1765 Sikh chiefs took Lahore, and three of them shared its rule for decades.

In 1799 the young Ranjit Singh rode into Lahore and made it the capital of a single Sikh Empire over the Punjab. After his death the British took the Punjab in 1849, and in 1947 Lahore went to Pakistan.
